names.legendary: Grainhalt, the Endless Afternoon

lore.common: Drops its last grain just after somebody declares the game finished.
lore.uncommon: Builds a tiny sand pyramid and insists it deserves a monument.
lore.rare: Slows its falling sand whenever the losing player looks hopeful. Entire board games have become diplomatic crises.
lore.epic: Swallowed every grain of sand on a crowded beach into its bottom bulb. The lifeguard now rents out the top bulb as an observation deck.
lore.legendary: A lonely child turned Grainhalt over at the beginning of summer and begged the afternoon not to end. Its sand has hovered in the centre ever since, and the picnic is still warm.

names.legendary: Saint Adhesia, Guardian of Tiny Heroes

lore.common: Sticks to everything except the small scratch it was supposed to cover.
lore.uncommon: Wears a cartoon dinosaur to persuade children that scraped knees are actually treasure maps.
lore.rare: Can mend a torn kite in a gale. Removing it afterwards requires a committee.
lore.epic: Covered an entire collapsing playground with one heroic stretch. The slide is now officially held together by a smiling cartoon frog.
lore.legendary: Once sealed a crack in a great dam with a single strip. Generations of engineers still leave little dinosaur stickers at the shrine.

names.legendary: Isobar, Judge of the Coming Storm

lore.common: Requires a little knock on the glass before agreeing what weather exists.
lore.uncommon: Wears a shiny brass face and judges your umbrella choices without saying a word.
lore.rare: Can summon rain by pointing at STORMY, usually when the school announces sports day.
lore.epic: Dropped its needle so low that the whole village anchored the washing line, the garden shed and one indignant goat.
lore.legendary: The storms themselves stand before Isobar for sentencing. One raised needle can pardon a hurricane; one sharp tap can condemn a picnic.

names.legendary: Reflexia, Witness of Roads Untravelled

lore.common: Folds itself in whenever a cyclist passes, like a shy metal ear.
lore.uncommon: Shows the cyclist behind you twice as close as reality. The driver learns humility quickly.
lore.rare: Sees dangers around corners and flashes warnings in the shape of tiny angry faces.
lore.epic: Reflected an entire convoy that had not yet arrived. The town built a welcome parade and accidentally welcomed itself.
lore.legendary: Reflexia remembers every road not taken and every near miss that never happened. In her silver face, travellers sometimes glimpse the lives they almost lived.

names.legendary: Aegis of the Thousand Sparks

lore.common: Gets knocked over by the cat and claims it was testing the fire alarm.
lore.uncommon: Its brass feet shine so brightly that the flames keep checking their reflections.
lore.rare: Catches escaping sparks like a goalkeeper. The chimney has started keeping score.
lore.epic: Blocked a shower of embers during the king's feast, then volleyed every spark safely up the chimney. The royal court applauded the fireplace.
lore.legendary: Aegis stood before the hearth when a thousand sparks tried to escape into the sleeping hall. Not one passed, and the old tapestry still bears the story in gold thread.

names.legendary: Sir Matchwell, the One-Inch Beacon

lore.common: Breaks when someone tries to strike it, then acts very surprised by its own strength.
lore.uncommon: Flares brighter than expected for one tiny instant and demands applause.
lore.rare: Builds miniature staircases from safe, unlit sticks leading directly to the biscuit tin.
lore.epic: Formed a tiny unlit timber bridge across the nursery floor so the toy soldiers could evacuate their castle.
lore.legendary: Sir Matchwell lit the way through an ancient cavern for a lost explorer, burning no faster than a firefly. When daylight came, the explorer found a little black crown of ash.

names.legendary: Old Milewarden, Keeper of the Road's End

lore.common: Clicks over one digit just as the driver starts wondering whether the journey will ever end.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to reset the holiday trip counter. Every visit to the shop now officially lasts four thousand miles.
lore.rare: Counts backward when the car reverses and convinces its owner the vehicle is getting younger.
lore.epic: Rolled through every digit at once on the motorway. The car declared itself brand-new and asked the mechanic for a birthday cake.
lore.legendary: Milewarden counted every road ever travelled by the wandering kings and kept their distances safe in its tiny wheels. The last number points toward a road that has not yet been built.

names.legendary: Sir Plungebold, Knight of the Lost Drain

lore.common: Makes a tremendously rude noise whenever it leaves the bathroom tiles.
lore.uncommon: Sticks to the sink and refuses to release its grip until the whole family applauds.
lore.rare: Pulls lost toys and wedding rings from drains without spilling a drop. The plumber is out of business.
lore.epic: Wrestled an entire bathtub free of its pipes while chasing a stubborn clog. The bath is now in the hallway with its rubber duck still aboard.
lore.legendary: Sir Plungebold descended into the ancient city's blocked waterways and freed a spring buried for centuries. The fountains erupted, and he emerged wearing a crown of soap bubbles.

names.legendary: Tripodax, the Third Leg of the Sky

lore.common: Extends two legs perfectly and jams the third in the wrong place.
lore.uncommon: Collapses only when everyone has finally lined up for the group photo.
lore.rare: Stands motionless through an earthquake and captures a perfectly sharp photograph of the disaster.
lore.epic: Planted its three legs across an entire mountain gorge to hold the camera of a giant wildlife photographer. The goats refused to pose.
lore.legendary: Tripodax stood beneath the oldest stars for ten thousand nights and never once trembled. Astronomers believe its three feet have pinned the very horizon in place.

names.legendary: Speculara, Queen Behind the Glass

lore.common: Waits until you smile for the bathroom selfie, then reveals toothpaste on your chin.
lore.uncommon: Copies every face perfectly except the eyebrows. It says those are an artistic choice.
lore.rare: Holds a second version of the room behind the glass. The cat has spent three years trying to evict its reflection.
lore.epic: Let every reflection in the dance studio step out for one rehearsal. They were better dancers and absolutely unbearable about it.
lore.legendary: Speculara collected the reflections of forgotten kings and kept them inside an endless silver hall. Once a century she lets one out to see whether the world remembers its face.

names.legendary: Oscillord, Reader of the Silent Pulse

lore.common: Shows a wiggly green line and judges anyone who admits they do not understand it.
lore.uncommon: Has so many dials that its owner needs a second machine to explain the first.
lore.rare: Hears a broken circuit's faint pulse and points to the precise screw that is misbehaving.
lore.epic: Drew a thunderstorm on its screen before the clouds arrived. The entire science club ran outside with umbrellas and received a standing ovation from lightning.
lore.legendary: Oscillord once measured the heartbeat of a sleeping mountain and discovered it was dreaming in radio waves. The village still receives strange lullabies at midnight.

names.legendary: Errandella, The Bag That Came Home

lore.common: Rustles during quiet moments and disappears beneath the sink with forty-seven relatives.
lore.uncommon: Collects every other shopping bag in the kitchen cupboard. It is building a very noisy family.
lore.rare: Floats on a breeze over three streets and lands neatly outside the shop its owner forgot to visit.
lore.epic: Joined with a hundred loose bags to form a huge floating supermarket whale. The town chased it with trolleys until it returned their groceries.
lore.legendary: Errandella was carried by a storm across the sea and returned a year later holding the same bread, fresh as the day it was bought. Nobody could explain the receipt.

names.legendary: Chronotick, the Ten Millionth Step

lore.common: Congratulates you for standing up to find the remote.
lore.uncommon: Sends a reminder to breathe whenever you're already breathing.
lore.rare: Announces everyone's terrible sleep at breakfast with impeccable timing.
lore.epic: Ordered the entire stadium to take ten thousand steps during the national anthem. Spectators marched halfway to the next town.
lore.legendary: Counted every footstep of a lost traveller across the desert. At the final step, its tiny screen lit up with the word HOME and a path through the dunes.

names.legendary: Scrollos, the Roll That Outlasted Time

lore.common: Clings to the wall with one stubborn square when the rest has disappeared.
lore.uncommon: Unspools across the floor just as the cat spots it.
lore.rare: Winds itself around a burglar's ankles and leaves a trail of paper clues straight to the police station.
lore.epic: Wrapped a three-storey hotel in a single enormous spiral of paper. Guests escaped through windows cut like little advent calendars.
lore.legendary: Scrollos was spun from the last cloud of an ancient summer and has never reached its cardboard middle. Monks have debated which way to hang it for nine centuries.

names.legendary: Binnith, the Mouth Beneath the Alley

lore.common: Slams its lid every time the wind tries to go to sleep.
lore.uncommon: Keeps an audience of flies that applaud whenever leftovers arrive.
lore.rare: Snaps its lid shut at the sight of a fox, then taunts it with the smell of leftover pizza.
lore.epic: Ate the entire town's rubbish after a festival and expanded into a towering metal beast with wheelie bins for armour.
lore.legendary: Binnith swallows everything abandoned in the alley, even forgotten names. On one moonless night each year, he burps up an enormous glowing collection of things their owners never knew they had lost.

names.legendary: Chronabelle, the Thirteenth Hour

lore.common: Ticks twice as loudly when the house is trying to sleep.
lore.uncommon: Runs five minutes fast just to watch everyone panic in the morning.
lore.rare: Slows the last ten minutes of school into a small eternity.
lore.epic: Stopped every clock in the town at the exact moment the mayor announced an early closing. Nobody has worked a Friday afternoon since.
lore.legendary: Once struck thirteen in a room with no windows. Everyone gained an hour to say the things they had never found time to tell each other.

names.legendary: Venetia, Mistress of the Stolen Dawn

lore.common: Tangling its own slats is its favourite morning exercise. Untangling them is yours.
lore.uncommon: Pull the cord once and it goes up. Pull it again and it rotates into a shape unknown to geometry.
lore.rare: Slices sunlight into striped prison bars across the sleeping cat. The cat considers it a personal attack.
lore.epic: Snapped open every blind on the street at once during a sleepover. A thousand teenagers saw the sun for the first time that year.
lore.legendary: Venetia can close the shutters on an entire sunrise. Kings once begged her for longer nights; bakers still consider her an enemy of civilisation.

names.legendary: Velouria, Keeper of the Unseen Stage

lore.common: Drops off one hook and hangs there looking tragically offended.
lore.uncommon: Hides children's feet so poorly that every game of hide-and-seek lasts eleven seconds.
lore.rare: Can conceal an entire doorway, a guilty expression or the neighbour's regrettable wallpaper.
lore.epic: Swept across the town theatre and swallowed the actors mid-speech. The audience gave the curtain a standing ovation.
lore.legendary: Was woven from the final twilight of a forgotten kingdom. Pull her closed, and even the oldest ghosts have somewhere private to weep.

names.legendary: Madame Veranda, Duchess of Summer

lore.common: Has two handles and a cruel sense of humour. The correct one changes every time guests arrive.
lore.uncommon: One half opens politely. The other half only opens when the guests have left.
lore.rare: Swings open to welcome butterflies, then locks the humans outside.
lore.epic: Opened during the midsummer dance and let the entire orchard wander into the drawing room. The guests applauded the moving scenery.
lore.legendary: Madame Veranda opens onto a perfect summer that lasts one afternoon each century. Visitors return with golden tans and very confused calendars.

names.legendary: Portadora, Guardian of the Last Welcome

lore.common: Slaps its letterbox shut whenever the postman says good morning. The postman has stopped being polite.
lore.uncommon: Won't open until the house key is turned while its owner whispers something nice about the hinges.
lore.rare: Shuts itself in front of uninvited guests but opens wide for the postman carrying pizza.
lore.epic: At the winter ball, it turned every knock into an announcement by a royal trumpeter. The guests arrived in full armour.
lore.legendary: Portadora once held shut the entrance to a haunted kingdom for a thousand years. It opened only when a lost child politely knocked and asked to borrow a torch.

names.legendary: Portcullis Pete, Keeper of the Cars

lore.common: Yawns upward each morning with a rumble loud enough to wake every bicycle on the street.
lore.uncommon: Opens whenever it hears a car horn, even if the car belongs to the neighbour.
lore.rare: Rolls itself upward so suddenly that a family of nesting pigeons gets an unexpected elevator ride.
lore.epic: Swallowed an entire garage sale behind its panels. Buyers spent the afternoon bargaining with a closed door.
lore.legendary: Portcullis Pete guards the last garage of a vanished city. Inside are a thousand lost bicycles, all perfectly oiled and waiting for their owners.

names.legendary: Vitrax, the Threshold of Two Worlds

lore.common: Holds its breath whenever somebody walks straight toward it. The forehead print is its favourite souvenir.
lore.uncommon: Collects little noseprints at exactly the height of curious children and extremely nosy dogs.
lore.rare: Its reflection waves half a second late, convincing a family there is someone else in the garden.
lore.epic: Became so invisible after cleaning that the entire town mistook its front entrance for an open doorway. The glass company's apology was delivered by a man with a sore nose.
lore.legendary: Vitrax shows not the room behind its glass, but the room you most wish to enter. For a thousand years, the keeper has stood guard to stop dreamers walking into the wrong life.

names.legendary: Curtainella, the Boundary of the Bath

lore.common: Clings to a leg like a desperate jellyfish whenever the extractor fan turns on.
lore.uncommon: Draws a new little smiley face in condensation after every hot shower.
lore.rare: Can hide an entire bathroom behind a single printed duck, confusing everyone looking for the soap.
lore.epic: Turned the morning shower into a raging pirate voyage. The shampoo bottles mutinied and the bath mat became a desert island.
lore.legendary: Curtainella hangs between the dry kingdom and the kingdom of water. Only those carrying a rubber duck may cross her folds without returning with soaked socks.

names.legendary: Noctivane, Lockkeeper of Dawn

lore.common: Bangs against the house at three in the morning as if it forgot its keys.
lore.uncommon: Houses a nest of sparrows who loudly object whenever someone opens it.
lore.rare: Closes faster than a gust can enter, keeping every candle lit through an enormous storm.
lore.epic: Slammed shut across a hundred seaside houses in one thunderclap. The town's seagulls dropped their stolen chips in surprise.
lore.legendary: Noctivane once sealed the night behind the shutters of a lighthouse so the sailors could rest. When dawn finally opened them, the sea itself applauded the keeper's patience.

names.legendary: Solaria, the Window Between Two Skies

lore.common: Drips cold rain onto the exact pillow someone has just fluffed.
lore.uncommon: Lets one curious star shine straight onto a sleeping child's nose every night.
lore.rare: Opens a clear patch in the clouds directly above the house whenever the family wants to watch meteors.
lore.epic: Caught an entire summer afternoon and spilled it into the winter attic. The houseplants held a party and forgot which season it was.
lore.legendary: Solaria was built to let the first dawn into a room that had forgotten the sun. Each night her glass shows a different constellation, including ones the astronomers insist have not been born.

names.legendary: Fenestria, the Window Between Seasons

lore.common: Refuses to open on hot days and swings wide during a blizzard.
lore.uncommon: Lets a fly in and spends the afternoon pretending it never noticed.
lore.rare: Shows a garden that changes with the seasons before they arrive.
lore.epic: Opened onto tomorrow during the school holidays. The children saw next week's homework and shut it immediately.
lore.legendary: Has one pane that looks into every place its owner has ever called home. At sunset it chooses the view they need most, usually somewhere with the lights on and supper ready.

names.legendary: Vitralis, the Unbreakable Crystal

lore.common: Rattles whenever a truck drives past the house.
lore.uncommon: Collects little drops of condensation and draws faces on the sill.
lore.rare: Shapes morning frost into maps of places nobody has visited.
lore.epic: Withstood a storm of hailstones as large as apples, catching one perfect shard in its glass. The family kept it in the freezer as a trophy.
lore.legendary: Reflected a thousand winters without cracking, even when the city around it crumbled. At last it was placed in a new home's window, where the first morning light shone through unbroken.

names.legendary: Seraphina, the Endless Binding

lore.common: Leaves a white trail down the hallway whenever it gets excited. The cat follows it solemnly.
lore.uncommon: Wraps a finger twelve times for a splinter. Calls this proper defensive strategy.
lore.rare: Can turn a playground pirate into an ancient mummy before the lunch bell rings.
lore.epic: Unfurled across a frozen river and wrapped the whole ice bridge before it cracked. The skaters sent a thank-you card.
lore.legendary: Her silver-white ribbons have bound shattered castles and guarded sleeping giants. She still gets tangled on door handles.

names.legendary: Speculara, Oracle of the Morning Face

lore.common: Steams up the moment somebody wants to check their hair. It enjoys suspense.
lore.uncommon: Keeps yesterday's finger-drawn messages hidden until the shower runs again.
lore.rare: Shows tomorrow's hairstyle today. The news is rarely encouraging.
lore.epic: Reflected every person in the house with the same ridiculous moustache. Nobody could prove who started it.
lore.legendary: A silver oracle that sees every possible face you could have worn. It has refused to reveal the one you will make when you meet your destiny.

names.legendary: Archimedes Jr, Keeper of the Last Drop

lore.common: Spills exactly one drop over the rim whenever the scientist looks away.
lore.uncommon: Claims its painted measurements are accurate. The school volcano disagrees.
lore.rare: Can hold a whole bucket of liquid without moving above the 100 ml mark. The chemistry teacher has questions.
lore.epic: Measured the school pond, a thundercloud and the headteacher's patience in one afternoon. Only the patience overflowed.
lore.legendary: Contains the very first drop of rain. Whoever pours it out can call a storm, but the beaker insists on an accurate measurement first.

names.legendary: His Royal Flushness, the Heated Seat

lore.common: Has twelve mysterious buttons and invites visitors to pick one. The danger is entirely psychological.
lore.uncommon: Makes an unexpected little splash whenever someone tries the control labelled GENTLE.
lore.rare: Heats itself so perfectly that the bathroom develops a waiting list.
lore.epic: Held the hotel hostage with its remote control. Every visitor received an unsolicited spa treatment and a polite apology.
lore.legendary: His luxurious throne knows every setting from warm breeze to royal fanfare. Ancient kings conquered continents for less comfort than his heated cushion.

names.legendary: The Black Maw, Collector of Everything

lore.common: Drips an unidentifiable liquid onto the only clean trousers in the house.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to close once full. Wears the last empty yogurt pot as a jaunty hat.
lore.rare: Gets a little bigger every time someone says JUST ONE MORE THING. The deckchair is next.
lore.epic: Swallowed the entire town's rubbish overnight and waddled to the collection point. The council gave it an employee badge.
lore.legendary: A vast black sack whose bottom has never been found. Whole civilizations of missing lids and single socks thrive somewhere in its folds.

names.legendary: Cordelia, Keeper of the Distant Gaze

lore.common: Rubs the back of the neck on every walk. It says the binoculars are just extremely affectionate.
lore.uncommon: Ties itself into a knot whenever a rare bird appears. The bird always laughs first.
lore.rare: Can swing a pair of binoculars around a cliff and catch them again, usually at the worst possible moment.
lore.epic: Snared a falling telescope from the edge of an observatory. The astronomers now call it their finest piece of equipment.
lore.legendary: For a thousand years Cordelia has kept the world's great watchers from losing their sighting tools. She never lets go, even when the stars move.

names.legendary: The Allseeing Piermaster

lore.common: Swallows a coin and immediately points at the least interesting cloud in the sky.
lore.uncommon: Stares over the sea all day and insists the same seagull has been spying on it for years.
lore.rare: Can read the labels on sandwiches across the Channel. Seagulls pay it for intelligence.
lore.epic: Swivelled toward the ice-cream van and projected the menu onto the clouds. The entire beach joined the queue.
lore.legendary: A weathered iron watcher with both eyes on the world's edge. Every ship it has ever watched return is marked by a new star in its lenses.

names.legendary: The Hundred Flames of Neverending June

lore.common: Reignite together just as the birthday child runs out of breath. The relatives demand a rematch.
lore.uncommon: Melt into the icing until every slice tastes like somebody's age.
lore.rare: Grant one wish only if every flame is extinguished. They consider fans cheating.
lore.epic: Lit the great-grandmother's cake so brightly that astronauts reported a new city. The smoke alarm performed Happy Birthday in Morse code.
lore.legendary: Each candle is a stolen year of youth. When the Hundred Flames burn together, clocks stop counting birthdays and the cake demands to be addressed as Your Majesty.

names.legendary: Cindermoor, Keeper of the Ancient Flame

lore.common: Sends smoke directly into your face regardless of where you move your chair.
lore.uncommon: Spits a spark every time someone says the fire looks safe. It loves dramatic irony.
lore.rare: Breathes out clouds that become miniature storms. Weather stations have stopped taking it seriously.
lore.epic: Crackled with such ferocity that the village fireworks fell respectfully silent. Then the marshmallows formed a protective union.
lore.legendary: For a thousand autumns, Cindermoor has guarded the ember no rain can quench. Even ghosts gather around it to warm their hands.

names.legendary: Ashenbriar, Keeper of the First Flame

lore.common: Toasts a marshmallow on one side and turns the other into a mysterious black pebble.
lore.uncommon: Pops loudly at the scariest part of any story. It has excellent timing and no conscience.
lore.rare: Whispers stories from the wood it burns. One log claimed to have been a pirate ship.
lore.epic: Summoned an entire forest of glowing sparks into the night sky. Campers thought the stars had come down to roast sausages.
lore.legendary: Ashenbriar holds the ember that warmed the first lost traveller. It will burn forever for anyone truly cold, although it still incinerates every marshmallow.

names.legendary: Chronoknight, Keeper of the Last Move

lore.common: Ticks twice as loud when somebody starts thinking. It knows exactly what it's doing.
lore.uncommon: Drops its little red flag the moment a player reaches for a winning piece.
lore.rare: Steals five seconds whenever someone says just one more move. Its collection fills an entire hourglass.
lore.epic: Accelerated the national chess final until both players were moving faster than the cameras. The referee declared the clock the winner.
lore.legendary: Chronoknight holds a single second that has never passed. Every grandmaster has begged for it; he grants it only to players brave enough to sacrifice their queen.

names.legendary: Dame Reflectrix, the Moonlit Clasp

lore.common: Opens itself in handbags and decorates everything with face powder. Calls it a makeover.
lore.uncommon: Shows one normal reflection and one with a nose the size of a turnip. Guess which one it prefers.
lore.rare: Can reflect the true face behind any disguise. Masquerade parties consider it a security risk.
lore.epic: Fired a sunbeam from its tiny polished lid that swept a foggy harbour clear for one glorious minute. The lighthouse asked for lessons.
lore.legendary: Dame Reflectrix carries a secret mirror polished from moonlight. It reveals the promises people made to themselves and forgot, which is why nobody opens her case at reunions.

names.legendary: Humus Rex, King Beneath the Soil

lore.common: Eats banana skins and belches the unmistakable perfume of personal failure.
lore.uncommon: Hosts worm banquets where the guests are also the cutlery.
lore.rare: Turns the neighbour's garden waste into prize-winning roses, then sends the invoice.
lore.epic: Ate the mayor's expensive lawn and returned it as a jungle. The mayor lost reelection to a tomato.
lore.legendary: Every forest grows from the banquet in Humus Rex's belly. Once a century it burps a new orchard, complete with a suspiciously familiar garden gnome.

names.legendary: Papyrion, Keeper of Abandoned Genius

lore.common: Misses the bin even when thrown from directly above it.
lore.uncommon: Unfolds itself and displays the shopping list everyone swore they didn't need.
lore.rare: Turns every discarded draft into an anonymous note to the boss.
lore.epic: Escaped the wastebasket as a storm of rejected homework. The school board was forced to read every excuse aloud.
lore.legendary: Was once a poem the world wasn't ready for. Centuries later, its creases contain the only map to the vanished Library of Unfinished Ideas.

names.legendary: Chronocuck, Herald of the Stolen Hour

lore.common: Shouts its name one time too many. The neighbours have counted.
lore.uncommon: Sneaks out early just to frighten the cat. The cat now wears a watch.
lore.rare: Announces tomorrow's hour today, causing widespread confusion at breakfast.
lore.epic: Sang thirteen at noon and sent the whole village into an argument with the calendar.
lore.legendary: Every midnight Chronocuck steals a single second and hides it inside its wooden heart. It plans to buy an entire extra day when it has enough.

names.legendary: Chronoshriek, Tyrant of the First Hour

lore.common: Flashes 12:00 for months after a power cut. It considers this artistic freedom.
lore.uncommon: Grants nine extra minutes of sleep, then collects the debt with compound interest.
lore.rare: Rings with the sound of your boss asking where you are. Horrifyingly effective.
lore.epic: Woke every household in the city at four in the morning for a meeting that didn't exist. By sunrise the citizens had outlawed alarm clocks.
lore.legendary: Once rang so loudly that dawn arrived before midnight just to silence it. The sun filed a formal complaint and Chronoshriek set a second alarm.

names.legendary: Portarius, Keeper of Every Threshold

lore.common: Only turns after both hands are completely full.
lore.uncommon: Gets inexplicably warm whenever somebody brings embarrassing news.
lore.rare: Can open any locked door except the bathroom when somebody is desperate.
lore.epic: Rearranged every door in the castle overnight. The king woke in the stable and the horses held a cabinet meeting.
lore.legendary: Portarius guards the line between welcome and unwelcome. Every door in the old kingdom once opened at its touch, except the one behind which it hid its own heart.

names.legendary: Thunderal, Lion of the Last Door

lore.common: Knocks when there is nobody outside. Finds the ensuing panic delightful.
lore.uncommon: Wears a brass lion's face to look intimidating. Is terrified of the milkman.
lore.rare: Its three knocks echo through every corridor, summoning guests from rooms that do not exist.
lore.epic: Rang the castle gate once and woke every ancestor in the royal portraits. They demanded to know why the furniture had changed.
lore.legendary: The last unopened gate of the forgotten city bears Thunderal's face. It knocks only for those who have a true story worth telling.

names.legendary: Orbiculus, Keeper of the Secret Turn

lore.common: Falls off whenever somebody says they have fixed it.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to turn clockwise on Tuesdays. Claims it is a personal boundary.
lore.rare: Lets cats open the door but turns into a solid brass boulder for humans.
lore.epic: Spun every doorknob in the palace at once, trapping the royal guests in an accidental game of musical rooms.
lore.legendary: Orbiculus knows the exact turn that opens every hidden door. For a thousand years treasure hunters have tried to bribe it; it accepts only perfectly polished fingerprints.

names.legendary: Garboth, King of Forgotten Things

lore.common: Opens its lid when nobody is around, just to scare pigeons.
lore.uncommon: Holds a dinner party for the local raccoons. Dress code is strictly optional.
lore.rare: Can swallow an entire sofa and burp out its lost remote.
lore.epic: Declared war on the city's rubbish collectors and built an army of discarded shopping trolleys. The mayor negotiated with a packet of biscuits.
lore.legendary: Garboth's kingdom lies beneath every landfill, where forgotten belongings are given new lives. The emperor's long-lost crown currently serves as a soup bowl.

names.legendary: Elevathor of the Thirteenth Floor

lore.common: Plays one cheerful tune while delivering everyone to the wrong floor.
lore.uncommon: Presses every button after the passengers have agreed not to. Denies having fingers.
lore.rare: Offers a secret floor to anyone brave enough to press thirteen. The doors open onto the office Christmas party from 1987.
lore.epic: Carried the entire building's workforce to the roof at once and refused to descend until somebody complimented its music.
lore.legendary: A thirteenth floor appears only when the building sleeps. Elevathor takes lost ambitions up there, gives them a desk and promotes them to management.

names.legendary: Hearthos, Guardian of the Final Spark

lore.common: Refuses to light the one log everyone has been staring at.
lore.uncommon: Warms the front of every person while their backs plot revenge.
lore.rare: Attracts every cat within three gardens. The local cats have formed a cosy committee.
lore.epic: Kept the winter festival so warm that the snowmen queued to get closer. The organisers finally moved the party into a paddling pool.
lore.legendary: Hearthos guarded one ember through the longest night in recorded history. When spring returned, it lit the village's first fire and demanded marshmallows as payment.

names.legendary: The Ancient Hearth of Lost Winters

lore.common: Sends one puff of soot onto the cleanest rug in the house.
lore.uncommon: Whispers through the chimney whenever the wind tells a good ghost story.
lore.rare: Keeps a stubborn ember alive long after the family has gone to bed.
lore.epic: Opened its chimney like a great stone throat during a snowstorm and sang an old winter song. Every house on the street began humming through its flue.
lore.legendary: Before the village had a name, the Ancient Hearth warmed its first travellers. The stones remember their stories and sometimes crackle with laughter when nobody is watching.

names.legendary: Pyrostellis, the Night Sky's Jester

lore.common: Has a magnificent picture on the box and produces one embarrassed squeak.
lore.uncommon: Launches with a dramatic hiss and appears to have forgotten the rest of the plan.
lore.rare: Can paint a glowing peacock across the sky. The real peacocks are furious.
lore.epic: Wrote HAPPY BIRTHDAY across the clouds in sparks, then misspelled the mayor's name so spectacularly that the town voted to rename him.
lore.legendary: Pyrostellis once challenged the constellations to an art contest and painted a dragon between the stars. The dragon liked its new home and still visits every New Year's Eve.

names.legendary: Sister Bandagella of the Healing Shelf

lore.common: Holds six kinds of plaster and none shaped like a knee.
lore.uncommon: Keeps the little scissors behind the gauze and denies they ever existed.
lore.rare: Produces exactly the dressing needed, but asks for a very detailed account of how the accident happened.
lore.epic: Opened itself at the school sports day and sent a squad of self-folding bandages racing down the track. The relay team lost to a roll of gauze.
lore.legendary: Bandagella patched the sails of a storm-torn rescue ship with its last strips of bandage. The sailors returned safely and built it a tiny cabinet with a sea view.

names.legendary: Medic Mitzi, Healer of the High Pass

lore.common: Keeps fifty plasters but not one for the particular finger that needs it.
lore.uncommon: Unrolls its bandage the full length of the kitchen and then asks for help folding it.
lore.rare: Appears in every family bag at once, except the bag containing the sandwiches.
lore.epic: At the mountain festival, its bandages flew into the wind and wrapped every sheep in a neat white bow. The farmer entered them in the costume competition.
lore.legendary: Mitzi travelled the oldest mountain trails without ever losing a traveller. Its little red cross became the sign that help was near, even in the deepest snow.

names.legendary: Ignis, the Last Light at Sea

lore.common: Lights up brighter than the picnic torch and expects an audience.
lore.uncommon: Covers the rescue boat in red smoke until the captain's hat looks like a tomato.
lore.rare: Burns beneath dark waves to guide a lost diver. The fish line up to read by it.
lore.epic: Blazed across a fogbound bay, guiding three stranded fishing boats home. The lighthouse complained it had been upstaged and requested a brighter bulb.
lore.legendary: Ignis rose above a black ocean when every star had disappeared. The sailors followed its single red flame to shore and named the safe harbour after it.

names.legendary: Mirroria, Keeper of the Other You

lore.common: Demands one more outfit check before anybody leaves the house. Nobody has ever passed on the first try.
lore.uncommon: Shows yesterday's hairstyle with alarming accuracy. Nobody has forgiven it.
lore.rare: Makes everyone look taller, except the person who paid extra for a long mirror.
lore.epic: Reflected an entire royal procession into an empty hallway. The king spent an hour bowing to himself.
lore.legendary: They say Mirroria holds the reflections of everyone who ever looked into it. Sometimes, after midnight, one reflection refuses to go home.

names.legendary: Globulus, Keeper of the Tiny Earth

lore.common: Spins until its countries blur together and refuses to stop on any place where the homework is due.
lore.uncommon: Spins until everybody gets dizzy and then insists it is the planet's fault.
lore.rare: Spins its miniature continents to rearrange actual holiday destinations. Last Tuesday every train to Italy arrived in Iceland.
lore.epic: Escaped the geography room and rolled through the capital, rearranging everyone's maps. Tourism numbers have never recovered.
lore.legendary: Globulus keeps a miniature world inside its painted shell. When the real Earth shakes, it gently steadies its little continents with one patient finger.

names.legendary: Chronopapa, Keeper of the Lost Hour

lore.common: Bongs when everyone is finally asleep. Claims its job description says nothing about kindness.
lore.uncommon: Needs winding every Sunday and spends Monday complaining that nobody appreciates the effort.
lore.rare: Swings its pendulum so steadily that visitors accidentally spend their entire afternoon nodding along.
lore.epic: Struck thirteen at midnight and convinced the village that tomorrow had arrived early. The bakers opened their shops in their pyjamas.
lore.legendary: At the end of every century, Chronopapa hides one hour inside its wooden case. A lucky child once opened the door and found an entire extra birthday.

names.legendary: Olibana, Weaver of Forgotten Fragrance

lore.common: Sends its smoke toward the one person who says they don't like smoke.
lore.uncommon: Fills the room with so much sandalwood scent that even the curtains start meditating.
lore.rare: Changes its fragrance to match every visitor's secret favourite place. The cat always smells fish.
lore.epic: Filled a grand palace with fragrant mist until the statues began dancing in the haze. The royal guards joined in.
lore.legendary: Olibana keeps the last scents of vanished gardens within her smoke. For one breath at dusk, she can bring a forgotten orchard back to life.

names.legendary: Puffbelle, Guardian of the Clear Air

lore.common: Lives in the school bag and rattles to remind its owner it's still there.
lore.uncommon: Gives a tiny encouraging shake before a difficult climb.
lore.rare: Summons a cool, gentle breeze when breathing becomes hard, helping its owner catch their breath.
lore.epic: Helped a determined runner through a stormy school race. The finishing ribbon lifted itself as she crossed, as though the wind were cheering too.
lore.legendary: Puffbelle carries a little pocket of spring air wherever her owner travels. Legends say she once returned a mountain singer's voice in the middle of an icy night.

names.legendary: Ocularis, Eye of the Locked House

lore.common: Watches the hallway through its tiny brass eye. It pretends the coat rack is fascinating.
lore.uncommon: Moves a millimetre to the left whenever the owner comes home in the dark.
lore.rare: Whistles so eerily through an old wooden door that the ghost inside has started charging it rent.
lore.epic: Refused every key in the castle on coronation day. The queen was crowned through the letterbox while the guests applauded from outside.
lore.legendary: Ocularis sees the last person who will ever unlock each door. It has kept one ancient doorway shut for centuries, waiting for a visitor who hasn't been born yet.

names.legendary: Flaskandra, Alchemist of Impossible Hues

lore.common: Swallows the cleaning brush and refuses to let it leave without a formal apology.
lore.uncommon: Makes every liquid swirl into a tiny whirlpool, including the teacher's tea.
lore.rare: Mixes two ordinary colours and invents a third that nobody can name.
lore.epic: Bubbled through the school science fair and filled the hall with a cloud of purple foam. The volcano exhibits requested a transfer.
lore.legendary: Flaskandra distilled a colour that exists only at the moment between sunrise and morning. Every artist who has tried to paint it discovers a new shade instead.

names.legendary: Nevergone, King of Forgotten Things

lore.common: Attracts seagulls from three counties with the scent of one old sandwich.
lore.uncommon: Grows taller every week while the rubbish lorries insist they have hardly brought anything.
lore.rare: Reassembles broken objects into strange machines beneath its hills. The diggers have started finding clocks that run backwards.
lore.epic: Rose into a mountain so large the town held its annual hill-climbing race on it. The winner reached the summit carrying a sofa.
lore.legendary: Beneath the oldest landfill sleeps a city built from everything humanity threw away. On moonless nights its lost toys, broken clocks and forgotten letters glow in windows no one remembers making.

names.legendary: Ragamuffin, the Last Wrapper

lore.common: Blows into the one freshly swept garden on the street. Calls it a housewarming gift.
lore.uncommon: Hides among the hedge leaves and rattles whenever a litter picker passes.
lore.rare: Climbs back out of the bin before its lid has closed. The park keeper has started negotiating.
lore.epic: Raised an army of crisp packets and marched across the football pitch, scoring the winning goal with a yoghurt lid.
lore.legendary: Ragamuffin survived seven storms, six recycling days and a furious street sweeper. It finally settled down as the crown of a magpie king.

names.legendary: Madam Minutia, Keeper of Hidden Worlds

lore.common: Makes the shopping list look enormous while leaving the price tag conveniently tiny.
lore.uncommon: Enlarges every beetle on the pavement until the children give them names and tiny hats.
lore.rare: Reads the fine print on a contract aloud, including the bits the salesman hoped nobody would notice.
lore.epic: Magnified one ant so dramatically that the school declared a dinosaur sighting and the ant asked for its own museum.
lore.legendary: Madam Minutia sees entire civilisations living inside the dots over the letter i. Her greatest discovery was a tiny philosopher who asked her to stop staring.

names.legendary: Inspector Grandis, the All-Seeing Lens

lore.common: Makes the eye behind it look enormous, and the dog refuses to recognise its owner.
lore.uncommon: Finds fingerprints on every polished table. The family is now under investigation for eating biscuits.
lore.rare: Follows a trail of crumbs so tiny that even the guilty mouse is impressed.
lore.epic: Enlarged the fingerprints on the mayor's trophy until the entire town recognised the baker's icing-covered hand. The trophy was a cake.
lore.legendary: Inspector Grandis once discovered an entire forgotten kingdom in a raindrop. He solved its royal disappearance before the drop reached the ground.

names.legendary: Glimmera, the Mirror of True Applause

lore.common: Magnifies a single freckle into a continent and insists its owner has discovered something.
lore.uncommon: Keeps its ring of lights glowing so brightly that the dressing room needs sunglasses.
lore.rare: Shows a perfect face on one side and the face you make when nobody is looking on the other.
lore.epic: Flashed its bulbs during the theatre premiere and dazzled the entire audience into applauding before the curtain rose.
lore.legendary: Glimmera has reflected every performer who ever stood before her. In the final act, those lost faces return to sing an encore no living audience could forget.

names.legendary: Flintkin, the Flame That Would Not Bow

lore.common: Flares for half a second, then leaves a thread of smoke and a very annoyed grown-up.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to strike when damp, but happily rattles inside the box.
lore.rare: Lights a candle with such precision that not a drop of wax escapes.
lore.epic: Held a tiny flame through a sudden winter gale just long enough for the lighthouse keeper to relight his lantern.
lore.legendary: Flintkin was the last spark kept safe through the longest winter. From its little flame, the village lanterns were rekindled one by one beneath the returning stars.

names.legendary: Ignispip, the Flame That Guided Dawn

lore.common: Wobbles atop a carefully held match and goes out with the smallest puff.
lore.uncommon: Hides from the wind behind a grown-up's cupped hand.
lore.rare: Burns blue, violet or gold for the briefest moment, like a tiny birthday wish.
lore.epic: Refused to be blown out by a fierce gale until every candle in the mountain shelter had been lit.
lore.legendary: Ignispip's brief flame led a lost village safely through the dark on a stormy night. Long after it faded, a thousand small lanterns carried its light home.

names.legendary: Professor Minuscule, the Eye of Infinity

lore.common: Makes everyone squint one eye shut and bump their forehead against the eyepiece.
lore.uncommon: Changes the focus whenever its owner finally sees something interesting.
lore.rare: Reveals a bustling city of tiny creatures in a single drop of pond water.
lore.epic: Turned a forgotten lunch crumb into an enormous expedition, complete with a map, flag and a terrified science teacher.
lore.legendary: Professor Minuscule discovered a microscopic civilisation within a raindrop and spent a lifetime recording its history. By the time he finished, the drop had evaporated into legend.

names.legendary: Lord One-Eye, Arbiter of Good Manners

lore.common: Pops out whenever somebody raises an eyebrow. Its favourite victims are people pretending not to be surprised.
lore.uncommon: Falls into afternoon tea with such regularity that the cup is now considered its assigned seat.
lore.rare: Makes even a scruffy pigeon look like a retired professor. The pigeon has started correcting grammar.
lore.epic: Stared down the entire royal banquet until every guest began eating with the correct fork. Even the soup sat up straight.
lore.legendary: Lord One-Eye gazed through his single glass and saw every lie told at the king's feast. By dessert the court had confessed everything except who stole the pudding.

names.legendary: Doctor Mycelia, Mother of the Tiny

lore.common: Grows a suspicious furry dot and insists it is just a very small houseplant.
lore.uncommon: Makes little colonies in different colours and demands tiny fences between them.
lore.rare: Arranges bacteria into microscopic messages. Yesterday's specimen wrote CLEAN THE FRIDGE.
lore.epic: Filled the science laboratory with a glowing miniature jungle overnight. The teacher found a tiny swing hanging from the microscope.
lore.legendary: Doctor Mycelia cultivated a living city inside a single glass dish, complete with roads and a mayor. She still attends council meetings through the microscope.

names.legendary: Solwax, Flame of the Unbroken Vigil

lore.common: Burns a tunnel down its middle and fills itself with a private pool of wax.
lore.uncommon: Drips down its side until it resembles a snowman having a very difficult summer.
lore.rare: Leans its flame towards anyone telling a lie, making family dinners suspiciously dramatic.
lore.epic: Stayed alight through an open-window banquet while every other candle blew out. The storm outside began to look embarrassed.
lore.legendary: Solwax kept vigil beside a sealed mountain gate for three hundred winters. Its single undying flame guided the returning guardians when their kingdom finally woke.

names.legendary: Porta Rex of the Sacred Cubicle

lore.common: Locks itself whenever someone has only thirty seconds to spare.
lore.uncommon: Creates a queue even when the cubicle is empty. Nobody knows how.
lore.rare: Keeps its seat clean through an entire crowded festival, a feat previously believed impossible.
lore.epic: Stood at the centre of a muddy music festival while every other cubicle toppled in the storm. The crowd gave it a standing ovation.
lore.legendary: Porta Rex survived seven legendary festivals, three hurricanes and a travelling circus without running out of paper. Its blue door is still honoured as a sanctuary by desperate campers.

names.legendary: Saint Sanitaria of the Builder's Dawn

lore.common: Arrives by crane and leaves the whole building site waiting for its most important delivery.
lore.uncommon: Shows OCCUPIED even when empty, as though fiercely protecting its privacy.
lore.rare: Travels between construction sites and always remembers which workers prefer the quiet corner.
lore.epic: Remained upright while a storm carried off every temporary shed and gazebo. The builders gave it a medal and a wider path.
lore.legendary: Saint Sanitaria stood alone beside the workers who rebuilt a ruined city. For years it offered shelter during every storm, and the last bricklayer hung a little wreath on its sturdy door.

names.legendary: Sir Pottypop, Conqueror of Diapers

lore.common: Sits proudly in the middle of the lounge and demands applause for absolutely nothing.
lore.uncommon: Sings its victory tune when the cat sits on it, confusing the sticker chart.
lore.rare: Knows exactly when a toddler needs it and rolls across the hallway like a tiny emergency vehicle.
lore.epic: Declared a royal celebration after one successful visit. The entire neighbourhood received medals shaped like little toilets.
lore.legendary: Sir Pottypop ended the Great Diaper War by teaching a thousand toddlers the art of the tiny throne. The kingdom celebrated with a million golden stickers.

names.legendary: Pluviara, Witness of the First Rain

lore.common: Gets filled by one raindrop and immediately writes a weather report about it.
lore.uncommon: Counts each millimetre with enormous seriousness, even when a bird drinks half the evidence.
lore.rare: Predicts tomorrow's rain by changing the tiny numbers on its side overnight.
lore.epic: Measured a storm so vast that the weather bureau ran out of digits. The forecast simply read GOOD LUCK.
lore.legendary: Pluviara accurately counted every raindrop in the Great Storm. The weather forecaster accused her of cheating; she now sends him wet invoices.

names.legendary: Retrovista, Watcher of Roads Untravelled

lore.common: Tilts to show exactly the wrong angle whenever someone tries to reverse.
lore.uncommon: Reveals a suspicious passenger in the back seat. It is always a forgotten shopping bag.
lore.rare: Shows what passed behind the car ten minutes ago, including the ice-cream van everyone missed.
lore.epic: Reflected every driver's worst parking attempt onto the clouds above the motorway. The traffic jam lasted until the laughter stopped.
lore.legendary: Retrovista shows travellers the road they did not take. Long ago its reflection guided a lost caravan away from an avalanche that had not yet fallen.

names.legendary: Moundmancer, Hoarder of Second Chances

lore.common: Grows another broken chair every time somebody claims the garage is finally tidy.
lore.uncommon: Uses a discarded lampshade as a crown and a shoe as a royal coach.
lore.rare: Hides perfectly good treasures beneath old cables, and only shows them to people willing to get their hands dirty.
lore.epic: Rose from the landfill like a mountain of forgotten furniture. By sunset it had built itself a palace from broken wardrobes.
lore.legendary: Moundmancer collects everything that people throw away too soon. On the night of the Great Repair, he returned a million broken toys to their owners, all laughing again.

names.legendary: Chronosand, Keeper of the Last Grain

lore.common: Runs out of sand exactly when the boiled egg still needs another minute.
lore.uncommon: Falls sideways and insists that time has now officially stopped for lunch.
lore.rare: Can steal five seconds from any argument. Nobody remembers who was winning.
lore.epic: Flipped itself at the school sports day and trapped the entire hundred-metre race inside one endless minute. The spectators finished their sandwiches twice.
lore.legendary: Chronosand holds one grain for every moment a promise has been kept. When the final grain falls, the world gains one perfect hour in which nobody is ever late.

names.legendary: Scentoria, Keeper of Summers Past

lore.common: Promises ocean breeze but makes the sitting room smell like lavender-flavoured toast.
lore.uncommon: Burns one minute before dinner and announces that the entire house is now a spa.
lore.rare: Releases the scent of somebody's happiest memory when its wick is lit. One family got the smell of wet dog.
lore.epic: Filled the city square with the scent of freshly baked biscuits. The bakeries sold out before anyone realised there were no biscuits.
lore.legendary: Scentoria captures the aromas of vanished seasons in a tiny amber flame. Once every hundred years she releases spring in midwinter, and even the stubborn trees remember how to bloom.

names.legendary: Skipthazar, the Bottomless Builder

lore.common: Gets filled with somebody else's old mattress before its owner has thrown away a single thing.
lore.uncommon: Accepts broken chairs at night and wakes up with a perfectly good bicycle.
lore.rare: Swallows a house renovation's entire debris pile and belches out exactly one missing door handle.
lore.epic: Devoured the demolished town hall in an afternoon. The builders found a miniature copy of it sitting neatly at the bottom.
lore.legendary: Skipthazar consumes the ruins of forgotten buildings and dreams them into new ones. Each morning an abandoned street wakes with one restored doorway and a strangely familiar letterbox.

names.legendary: Nivella of the Captive Winter

lore.common: Lives beneath a plastic pine tree and insists every shake is an earthquake drill.
lore.uncommon: Replaces its tiny snowman's carrot nose after every blizzard. Nobody knows where it gets carrots.
lore.rare: Traps whoever peers into its glass inside a miniature snowy town for exactly seven sneezes.
lore.epic: Shook the entire gift shop into a snowdrift, complete with a tiny chairlift operating between the shelves.
lore.legendary: Nivella keeps the last snowfall of an extinct kingdom under glass. Once a century she opens the dome to let one snowflake find its way home.

names.legendary: Cantrix, the Thousandth Rebirth

lore.common: Rattles along the kerb at three in the morning like a tiny percussion solo.
lore.uncommon: Gets flattened by a bicycle and pops back into shape, looking smug.
lore.rare: Convinces every discarded can in the street to follow it in a noisy silver procession.
lore.epic: Rolled into the recycling depot and led a tin-can revolt. By morning, the machines were making medals instead of cans.
lore.legendary: Cantrix remembers every life it has lived: bicycle frame, aeroplane wing, lunchbox, fizzy drink. Its greatest ambition is to become a bell and announce itself.

names.legendary: Pyrelle, Who Taught Stars to Write

lore.common: Tries to spell HAPPY BIRTHDAY in the air but runs out after HAPPY BIR.
lore.uncommon: Sprinkles tiny golden sparks over everyone's gloves and calls it a free decoration.
lore.rare: Draws glowing messages that hang in the night sky until morning, usually reminders to buy milk.
lore.epic: Wrote a blazing marriage proposal above the fireworks display. The whole town said yes before the intended person could answer.
lore.legendary: Pyrelle wrote the first constellation with a burning wand. Every meteor shower since is her impatient attempt to correct the spelling.

names.legendary: Horosol, the Shadow That Outlived Time

lore.common: Refuses to tell the time when the sky has even one cloud.
lore.uncommon: Makes its shadow point at tea time regardless of the hour.
lore.rare: Steals minutes from nearby clocks and hides them beneath the garden gnomes.
lore.epic: Cast its shadow across three kingdoms at the equinox, ending every royal speech at precisely the same instant.
lore.legendary: Horosol stood in the first garden before clocks were invented. At the final sunset it will mark one last hour that belongs to no one.

names.legendary: Serapha, the Gentle Healer

lore.common: Looks much scarier than it feels and secretly prefers bandages to needles.
lore.uncommon: Gives a tiny brave squeak whenever a patient looks away.
lore.rare: Makes the waiting room's nervousness vanish with one gentle tap; the sticker box has never been so popular.
lore.epic: Calmed a herd of frightened zoo elephants before their check-ups. The veterinarian ended the day wearing forty celebratory stickers.
lore.legendary: Serapha carried medicine across the mountain passes when every road was frozen, bringing relief in a tiny glass barrel. The villagers planted flowers along her trail.

names.legendary: Lucindel, Flame of the River Wishes

lore.common: Burns bravely for twenty minutes, then asks for a fresh little tin.
lore.uncommon: Floats inside a water bowl and insists it has joined the navy.
lore.rare: Jumps from lantern to lantern, leaving a glowing trail the moths follow like treasure hunters.
lore.epic: Set a hundred festival lanterns alight with one tiny flame, drawing a ribbon of floating stars across the river.
lore.legendary: Lucindel guards the wishes sent down the river in candlelit bowls. Her fire never consumes the paper bearing a promise, even when every other light has gone out.

names.legendary: Astrelion, Witness to the Unborn Star

lore.common: Points at a chimney and insists the soot is an exciting new constellation.
lore.uncommon: Shows the moon upside down, and the astronomers pretend this is the traditional view.
lore.rare: Tracks comets before they appear, then writes cheeky notes on the lens about their arrival times.
lore.epic: Focused on a distant nebula until its swirling colours spilled into the observatory and painted the dome from inside.
lore.legendary: Astrelion watched a new star gather from darkness over a million patient nights. When it finally kindled, he was the first to whisper its name.

names.legendary: Ampullion, Vessel of the First Element

lore.common: Rolls off the lab bench the moment its owner forgets the little wooden rack.
lore.uncommon: Fires its rubber bung at the teacher when the experiment gets particularly exciting.
lore.rare: Hatches tiny coloured creatures from harmless school experiments; the green one eats homework.
lore.epic: Grew a single rainbow bubble until it filled the chemistry laboratory and lifted every desk gently to the ceiling.
lore.legendary: Ampullion contains one clear drop from the dawn of matter. Every element glimpses its forgotten origin in the glass and glows with recognition.

names.legendary: Rackador of Twelve Worlds

lore.common: Has one hole too narrow for the fattest test tube and refuses to apologise.
lore.uncommon: Rattles its glass passengers like a tiny marching band during every experiment.
lore.rare: Sorts vials by the sounds their bubbling liquids make, composing a very odd symphony.
lore.epic: Carried a dozen runaway reactions across the science fair without losing a drop. The headteacher gave it the gold medal for bravery.
lore.legendary: Rackador holds twelve enchanted vessels, each containing a different miniature world. Every dawn it rearranges them so their inhabitants can exchange the sunrise.

names.legendary: Celsia, Healer of Heat and Cold

lore.common: Beeps the moment someone has finally stopped fidgeting.
lore.uncommon: Claims the bath is either too hot or too cold, never just right.
lore.rare: Reads a person's true mood alongside their temperature, leaving grumpy relatives with very embarrassing results.
lore.epic: Measured a heatwave so furious it demanded the sun report to the school nurse. The afternoon immediately cooled off.
lore.legendary: Celsia measured the last ember of warmth in a dying village and carried it to the smallest house. There she taught winter how to be gentle.

names.legendary: Aquacistern, the Heart Behind the Wall

lore.common: Makes a dramatic watery groan three minutes after everyone has gone to bed.
lore.uncommon: Fiddles its little float until the tank stops filling exactly when you need it.
lore.rare: Speaks through the pipes to other bathrooms, passing gossip in perfectly timed gurgles.
lore.epic: Drained and refilled a whole hotel on its own, sending a tidal wave of bubbles through a hundred unsuspecting toilets.
lore.legendary: Aquacistern lives behind the oldest palace wall, collecting the echoes of every whispered secret in the washroom. Its single midnight flush is said to reveal who stole the crown.

names.legendary: Spindelius, Ender of the Great Roll War

lore.common: Launches its spring-loaded spindle across the bathroom with a cheerful ping.
lore.uncommon: Stares at the empty cardboard tube, judging everyone who walks past.
lore.rare: Changes every roll to the correct direction before dawn, according to a rule only it knows.
lore.epic: Spun an entire household's supply into one giant paper cocoon, then appointed the family's bewildered cat as its guardian.
lore.legendary: Spindelius settled the centuries-old over-or-under dispute by placing a roll on every door in the kingdom. Nobody agreed, but everyone had plenty of paper.

names.legendary: Baaalina, the Porcelain Pasture

lore.common: Slips sideways the moment someone sits down, then acts innocent.
lore.uncommon: Looks so much like a tiny sheep that the dog keeps trying to herd it.
lore.rare: Sprouts soft wool whenever the bathroom is cold and refuses to let anyone leave without a warm seat.
lore.epic: Grew a flock of furry toilet-seat rings across an entire hotel. The sheepdog booked a room and called it heaven.
lore.legendary: Baaalina's fleece once softened the stone throne of a notoriously grumpy monarch. The king began smiling, while his royal shepherd spent the rest of his life guarding the bathroom.

names.legendary: Porcellus, the Tank of Seven Echoes

lore.common: Rattles its heavy lid whenever the bathroom door closes.
lore.uncommon: Keeps the water trickling all night and blames the goldfish.
lore.rare: Holds the flush hostage until someone jiggles a mysterious little lever three times.
lore.epic: Released a perfectly timed chorus of flushing tanks across the city during the mayor's speech. The audience applauded the plumbing.
lore.legendary: Porcellus sits atop an ancient labyrinth of pipes, and every flush sends seven different echoes to seven distant fountains. The one that answers back knows your forgotten name.

names.legendary: Ignivara, Flame of the Forgotten Watch

lore.common: Spits a little ash on whoever carries it down the corridor.
lore.uncommon: Whispers spooky stories through its crackling flame, mostly about the cellar.
lore.rare: Casts a giant armed shadow onto the castle wall and convinces intruders a guard is awake.
lore.epic: Lit every passage in an abandoned fortress at once, setting the suits of armour marching in their own enormous shadows.
lore.legendary: Ignivara was lit when the first castle swore to shelter travellers. Though every stone has since crumbled, her flame still appears on lonely roads whenever someone has lost their way.

names.legendary: Grimbag, the Sack of Unwanted Wishes

lore.common: Splits its bottom the instant someone says the bin run will be easy.
lore.uncommon: Ties its own drawstrings into a knot no human hand can untangle.
lore.rare: Sneaks out on bin night and comes back stuffed with objects everyone secretly misses.
lore.epic: Swelled with enough discarded party decorations to become a great wobbling monster that bounced through the town square wearing twelve paper hats.
lore.legendary: Grimbag collects every little thing someone throws away in anger. Once each winter it returns one lost treasure to its owner, wrapped in a ribbon made of old shopping receipts.

names.legendary: Gimbalora, the Eye That Never Shook

lore.common: Tilts down just as the photographer says everyone is in frame.
lore.uncommon: Twists its little lever at the wrong moment and photographs mostly ankles.
lore.rare: Turns a camera slowly towards secrets hidden beyond the edge of every ordinary picture.
lore.epic: Spun through a complete panorama and captured tomorrow's festival halfway around the mountain. The organisers had not even announced it.
lore.legendary: Gimbalora's enchanted bearing tracks the last thing a wanderer longs to see. Point a camera through her lens and the horizon itself turns to reveal the way home.

names.legendary: Urinaldo, the Fountain of Final Whistles

lore.common: Flushes itself whenever a passer-by thinks the bathroom is empty.
lore.uncommon: Guards a mysterious blue deodorant block like it is a precious jewel.
lore.rare: Adjusts its own height to suit each visitor and never admits how it does so.
lore.epic: Expanded the stadium loos into an impossible maze at half-time. Supporters emerged wearing the wrong team's scarves.
lore.legendary: Urinaldo presides over a secret network of stadium washrooms where every victory chant echoes forever. At the final whistle he turns the pipes into a brass fanfare that only the plumbing can hear.

names.legendary: Speculara, the Other Side of Morning

lore.common: Makes everyone check their hair before leaving, including the dog.
lore.uncommon: Collects fingerprints at the precise height of an enthusiastic selfie.
lore.rare: Shows the hallway as it looked yesterday, complete with evidence of who knocked over the flowers.
lore.epic: Refused to reflect anyone until they told the truth. The family reunion took considerably longer than expected.
lore.legendary: Preserves the reflection of one person who has not yet been born. When the child finally arrived, the mirror smiled for the first time in a hundred years.

names.legendary: Hearthus, the Winter's Old Friend

lore.common: Burps a puff of ash whenever somebody opens its little iron door.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to burn the last log until everyone compliments its glow.
lore.rare: Can roast chestnuts through its glass without scorching a single one, even when nobody tends the fire.
lore.epic: Baron Cindercoat warmed the whole snowbound village from one cottage chimney. The snowmen gathered at the door demanding equal treatment.
lore.legendary: When the mountain's last hearth went dark, Hearthus kept one ember asleep inside his iron belly for seven winters. He woke it for the first lost traveller, and the mountain road has never been lonely since.
